## 🎯 Content and goals

- You can choose the **right kind of AI system** for a given research task.
- You can write prompts that are **specifications**, not wishes.
- You can **verify** AI output to the standard your term paper is held to.
- You can **disclose** your use of AI so that it cannot be read as cheating.

Explicitly *not* a goal: knowing which app is currently best. The tools change
faster than a semester; the reasoning does not. The list of tools I currently
recommend is kept below, where it can be corrected quickly.

## 🧭 Tools I currently recommend

::: {.callout-note}
## This list is deliberately kept here rather than on the slides
Products change faster than a semester, so the slides teach the four
**capability classes** and this page names the products. Reorganised from the
2025 edition of the lecture by class.

**Last reviewed: August 2026.** If you are reading this much later, treat every
name below as a starting point for your own search, not as an endorsement.
:::

### A — Conversational assistants

Generating, restructuring, explaining and critiquing text and ideas.
Ungrounded by default.

- **Claude**, **ChatGPT**, **Gemini** — the general-purpose assistants. Any one
  of them is enough; there is little point in subscribing to several.
- **DeepSeek** — an open-weight alternative. Note that where the hosted service
  runs matters for the data-protection questions discussed in the lecture.

### B — Grounded search

Retrieving real sources and citing them. Always use a proper database
(Web of Science, Scopus) as the foundation and treat these as complements —
see [Lecture 08](l_08_LiteratureReviews.qmd).

- *Semantic tools ("finders")* — start from a question or topic description:
  **Elicit**, **Consensus**, **Undermind**, **SciSpace**.
- *Citation-based tools ("connectors")* — start from one or more seed
  publications and follow citation networks: **Connected Papers**,
  **ResearchRabbit**, **Inciteful**.
- **Perplexity** — general grounded search rather than an academic tool;
  useful for orientation, weaker for a systematic review.

A practical order that works: database first, then a semantic tool to widen the
net, then a citation-based tool once you have identified key publications.

### C — Document and data analysis

You supply the material — PDFs, transcripts, datasets — and the system reads
what you give it.

- The general assistants in class A now handle uploaded PDFs and datasets well,
  and have largely absorbed the single-purpose tools of a few years ago.
- **NotebookLM** — works only from sources you upload, which makes it easier to
  check what a claim rests on.
- **MaxQDA** — qualitative content analysis, with AI features added; relevant
  for [Lecture 06](l_06_Interviews.qmd) if you have access to a licence.
- Remember the confidentiality rule from the lecture: interview transcripts and
  unpublished firm data do not go into any of these without thinking first.

### D — Agentic systems

Planning and executing multi-step work — browsing, running code, producing
files. You review the trace, not only the answer.

- The agent modes of the class-A assistants are the realistic entry point.
- Useful for mechanical work with a **checkable** result. Not useful for
  anything where you could not tell a good result from a bad one.

### Not AI, but do not skip it

- **Zotero** — reference manager. Nothing on this page removes the need for
  one, and it is what keeps a fabricated reference from silently entering your
  bibliography.

### Also worth knowing

- The *Virtuelles Kompetenzzentrum KI* maintains a
  [curated list of AI tools](https://www.vkkiwa.de/ki-ressourcen/ki-tools/) that
  is updated more often than this page.

## ✍️ Exercises and coursework

*Suggested exercises (to help you remember the material; not graded):*

- Work through the [citation-checking exercise](ai-citation-check/index.qmd) if
  you were not in class, or repeat it on a paragraph you generate yourself.
- Take a prompt you have actually used and rewrite it as a specification —
  context, task, format, constraints — then compare the two outputs.
- Fill in the [disclosure template](ai-disclosure/index.qmd) for a piece of work
  you have already handed in. It is quicker than you expect, and much quicker
  than reconstructing it later.
